The current state-of-the-art focuses on benchmarking the operational performance of implementing PQC, but the real-world adoption status remains under-researched. This work utilizes large-scale SSH fingerprint data from a proprietary scanning tool to analyze PQC adoption across 1.52 million hosts and 27,012 entities. Our study shows that the PQC transition in the SSH protocol is underway but highly polarized: 45.2% of SSH hosts on port 22 support PQC, while 54.8% remain classical-only. At the entity level, 39.9% have enabled PQC on at least one host, whereas 60.1% have no PQC support. By correlating PQC adoption with industry, geography, and organizational size (digital and financial), this study provides a comprehensive empirical assessment of PQC adoption status in SSH infrastructure.

papers.title: Theory of Optical and Magneto-Optical Properties of [111]-Oriented Site-Controlled Quantum Dots
papers.abstract: Site-controlled [111]-oriented quantum dots (QDs) are promising sources of non-classical light, yet their optical spectra exhibit apparently conflicting symmetry signatures. At zero magnetic field, excitonic spectra are commonly interpreted as $C_{2v}$-like, whereas measurements in Faraday geometry display selection rules characteristic of $C_{3v}$-like symmetry. Here, we show that both regimes can be described consistently without invoking any change in the underlying structural symmetry. Combining 8-band $\mathbf{k}\cdot\mathbf{p}$ theory, a self-consistent Hartree-informed configuration interaction scheme, and group theoretical analysis, we introduce a controlled symmetry reducing perturbation that lowers the QD symmetry to $C_s$. At zero field, the optical response remains predominantly $C_{2v}$-like because the additional low-symmetry transitions carry only weak oscillator strengths. In Faraday geometry, the same reduced-symmetry structure produces four dominant, nearly circularly polarised trion transitions, reproducing the experimentally observed $C_{3v}$-like response. By contrast, an exact $C_{2v}$ description inferred from the zero-field spectrum permits only two such trion transitions and therefore fails at finite field. Our results thus provide a unified description of the zero and finite magnetic field optical response without any restoration or enhancement of the underlying structural symmetry. More generally, we demonstrate that a higher-symmetry-like optical spectrum does not uniquely identify the exact symmetry of a QD, therefore also providing useful guidance for other QD and nanostructure systems that lie beyond the ones studied here.

papers.title: Cavity-enhanced second harmonic generation from Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O
papers.abstract: Rydberg excitons in Cu$_2$O provide a solid-state setting for creating giant optical nonlinearities. Here, we use second-harmonic generation (SHG) to study Rydberg excitons in a doubly resonant optical microcavity designed to enhance both the pump and second-harmonic fields. We observe even-parity exciton states in an optical cavity and extend cavity-based measurements of Rydberg excitons up to $n=10$. The SHG intensity depends strongly on pump cavity detuning, showing the dominant role of the microcavity is the enhancement of the intra-cavity pump field. Analysis reveals an additional enhancement from the resonant second-harmonic cavity giving an overall SHG enhancement factor of $21 \pm 2$ inside the microcavity. These results establish cavity-enhanced SHG spectroscopy as a valuable tool for studying Rydberg excitons in microcavities and provide a pathway towards exploiting optical nonlinearities in Rydberg exciton polariton systems.

papers.title: Finite-time Cholesky Factorization
papers.abstract: We propose an algorithm for estimating the Cholesky factorization of positive, semi-definite matrices without pivoting. Our method has the same data access pattern as the canonical Cholesky method, and therefore is amenable to familiar hardware optimization techniques. Our method interprets the factorization task as a variational problem and in turn solves it using an induced dynamical system. We study the rate of convergence of this dynamical system to its stationary state for both positive definite and semi-definite matrices. Numerical experiments validate that our method is competitive with pivoted Cholesky on several practical examples.

papers.title: Empirical Assessment of Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption Status in TLS
papers.abstract: Anticipating Q-day security concerns, major CDNs and cloud providers are migrating to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). While existing literature benchmarks PQC performance, empirical research evaluating real-world adoption data remains scarce. We present an empirical assessment of PQC deployment across seven critical protocols (HTTPS, LDAPS, SMTPS, IMAP-SSL, POP3-SSL, TELNETS, and RDP) using 10,000 target IP addresses per protocol. At the origin-server level, PQC algorithm support reaches 9.1% for HTTPS and 7.39% for LDAPS, while falling below 1% for all other evaluated protocols. At the entity level, PQC support is 11% for HTTPS and 5.4% for LDAPS, while the remaining protocols have less than 5% of entities supporting PQC on the hosted servers. We further correlate these adoption trends against organizational digital and financial footprint, and industry sectors, yielding a multi-dimensional empirical assessment of PQC deployment. Finally, at the domain level, we perform a comparative analysis of PQC adoption in Cloudflare-hosted domains against baseline Cloudflare datasets. Collectively, our findings provide critical insights into the current state of PQC readiness over Transport Layer Security (TLS).

papers.title: A wearable input/output interface learns personalized models of haptic perception
papers.abstract: Wearable haptic interfaces deliver physical stimuli to the skin, yet perceived locations vary widely across users and diverge from actuator locations, particularly for emergent tactile-feedback techniques. We developed a wearable haptic input/output (I/O) device integrating a 36-channel electrotactile array with capacitive touch sensing, enabling stimulation and user-reported percept locations to be registered within the same body-referenced coordinate frame. In 24 participants, the device revealed electrotactile and referred-thermal perceptual maps with notable interparticipant variability. Despite this variability, both modalities retained electrode-pair-specific spatial structure across participants. Tactile and thermal percepts also showed spatial correspondence, whose strength varied across participants. These findings motivated our human-in-the-loop calibration framework, which adapts a forward-prediction strategy to individual users and generates personalized perceptual models. These models enabled inverse rendering by selecting stimulation patterns predicted to generate a target percept for a specific user. Using these models, we demonstrate personalized haptic rendering in haptic-guided robot teleoperation, visual-to-haptic sensory substitution, interpersonal haptic communication, and virtual reality (VR). Together, this platform provides a route toward adaptive haptic interfaces that measure, model, and render according to each user's perception.

papers.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
papers.abstract: RidgeFill shortens prefill by not computing most of a model's upper layers for the prompt. The lower layers run exactly up to a split; from the split layer's state a per-layer map predicts every later layer's input, and each late layer writes its cache from that prediction. The design follows YOCO and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, where the projection is trained into the model. RidgeFill retrofits it onto models that were never trained for it: the map is a ridge regression fitted once in closed form from one pass over calibration text, the layer's own projections run unchanged, and a chosen set of rows, the last few thousand tokens, and every decoding step run the full model. Nothing is trained and no token is dropped. Most of the work was in measurement, finding a repeatable methodology. Loss averaged over all tokens hides RidgeFill's error. Needle retrieval in the filled region, loss on tokens that depend on distant context, and splice tests that swap filled keys or values for exact ones show which component carries it: the keys on Llama-3.1-8B, half of it in their scale, and the values and the recurrent state on Qwen3.5-9B. On Qwen3.8-27B in a llama.cpp fork on an A100, time to first token is 1.25 to 1.31x faster at 16K to 120K tokens with the maps in VRAM; RULER changes by -1.2 and -1.4 points and LongBench v2 by -1.4; the 95 % intervals include zero but do not rule out losses of a few points. On Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in vLLM it is 1.50 to 1.60x faster than exact at 9K to 32K tokens, with RULER's needle tasks at 99.8 against 100.0 and perplexity on novel tokens 2.65 % higher [-0.02 %, +4.93 %]. On three 8 to 9B reference models, at the same split and tail as the identity fill, the fitted map retrieves 49.1 and 49.6 more filled-region RULER points on the two dense models (at that split Llama's loss is worse), and its long-document loss is +/-0.03 nats of the released SwiftKV checkpoint's.

papers.title: Slow structures, fast degrees of freedom, and the morphology of chess openings
papers.abstract: Chess openings naturally separate into slow and fast degrees of freedom: pawns evolve through irreversible moves, whereas pieces can be rapidly reorganized within the resulting structure. We exploit this separation to construct a quantitative morphology of opening space. From a catalogue of 3810 named variations, 1749 reach a common depth of $N=10$ plies, corresponding to 619 distinct positions and only 435 joint pawn structures. We characterize these positions through observables measuring pawn commitment and spatial organization, blockade and tension, and piece activity and centralization. Their partial independence reveals a multidimensional opening space and in order to explore its structural organization, we construct a network whose nodes are distinct White pawn structures, connected when a single pawn move or capture transforms one into another. Remarkably, 139 of the 149 observed structures belong to a single connected component containing $98\%$ of all positions. This network exhibits a statistically significant modular organization, with eight communities whose representative structures correspond to familiar pawn formations. Rather than forming isolated categories, these formations emerge as distinct regions of a connected structural landscape. Our approach thus complements the traditional opening taxonomy by revealing similarities between differently named openings and providing a quantitative basis for comparing the positions they produce.

papers.title: Euler trace congruences over local fields
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a finite extension of $\QQ_p$ with uniformizer $π$ and residue field $\FF_q$. For each $r\ge1$, we determine the largest integer $E_r$ such that $\Tr(A^{q^r})\equiv\Tr(A^{q^{r-1}})\pmod{π^{E_r}}$ for every integral matrix $A$ with a prescribed residual similarity class. We give formulas for both nilpotent and nonnilpotent residual classes and construct integral lifts attaining the resulting exponents. We also exhibit local fields with the same ramification index and residue field for which the optimal exponents differ, even when $r$ and the residual similarity class are fixed.

papers.title: ICare-DT: a digital twin for continuous forecasting of intensive care patients
papers.abstract: Digital twins of intensive care patients should update forecasts from new data and predict treatment responses, but few studies test whether routine records support either. We propose ICare-DT, a Transformer-based twin that updates a latent patient state hourly from new measurements without retraining. We trained it on 140,473 eICU-CRD stays to forecast vital signs crossing their training-set means. On test data, later forecasts beat the twin's own hour-6 forecasts of the same windows in all 12 settings (+0.073 to +0.153 AUROC). On validation data, controls that withheld or swapped the new hours traced the gain to the patient's own measurements. Without refitting, the model kept its gain on a second database (8 of 9 settings, +0.025 to +0.114 AUROC) in a prespecified evaluation of the previously analyzed MIMIC-IV test split. Refitted within MIMIC-IV, a twin state fine-tuned on clinical endpoints gave gradient boosting a significant gain for acute kidney injury (+0.0035 AUROC; hypotension +0.0010, not significant). To test response prediction, we built a benchmark that replaces the treatments in real records with simulated doses and injects responses of known size, visible only at measurement times. Ridge models supervised with injected effects recovered them from real records only through frequently measured variables (heart rate) read at their measurement times. We asked standard learners to predict these effects for a dosing regime no patient had received. No standard learner outperformed predicting zero effect at an out-of-support query. When told how the simulated responses were generated, a separate learner recovered the effects from the same records without seeing their true values (R2 0.30 to 0.40 at one effect size). Routine records support forecasts that improve with each patient's new data, and our benchmark is a testbed for models that learn how responses are generated.

papers.title: Shaping Frequency-Bin Biphoton Correlations via Programmable Optical Frequency Combs
papers.abstract: Programmable shaping of photon-pair spectral correlations is important for frequency-bin quantum information processing. However, achieving this control remains challenging in nonlinear optical systems without reliable forward models. Here, we demonstrate model-free, hardware-in-the-loop shaping of the measured joint spectral intensity of a cascaded photon-pair source driven by a programmable optical frequency comb. A blockwise simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation controller optimizes up to 22 pump, signal, and idler parameters. Each iteration requires only two accepted hardware evaluations, independent of the parameter count. The controller converges to diverse target patterns on 3$\times$3, 4$\times$4, and 5$\times$5 frequency-bin grids. The optimized distributions achieve Pearson correlations between 0.66 and 0.98 and classical overlap fidelities between 0.32 and 0.62. Cross-target similarity analysis confirms that the optimized patterns remain target-specific. Source characterization yields a maximum coincidence-to-accidental ratio of approximately 585. Accuracy is limited by pump-phase transfer, parasitic nonlinear background, waveshaper constraints, amplitude-only filtering, and measurement noise. Joint spectral intensity contains no spectral-phase information. Therefore, the results demonstrate control of measured frequency-bin populations and correlations, not complete reconstruction of the two-photon state. Phase-sensitive characterization is required to verify inter-bin coherence and quantify the entanglement dimensionality of the output state. Our results establish direct measurement feedback as a practical approach to reconfigurable frequency-bin correlation engineering when an accurate end-to-end model is unavailable.

papers.title: Adapting Frozen Promptable Segmenters to User-Defined Taxonomies via Few-Shot Proposal Learning
papers.abstract: Promptable segmenters of the SAM family turn a click or a phrase into an instance mask, so the costly part of a label is now its class. However, each annotation project draws its own class boundary, often through objects these models already know: people from cars, sedans from trucks, one sedan model from another. A generic model's boundary is fixed by its training vocabulary. We present SNAP, an annotation pipeline that learns the project's boundary from the labels the annotator draws anyway. On one frozen SAM2.1 pass per image, we fit a per-project head, SnapHead, that classifies every proposal and refits in seconds after each labeled image. Where SAM 3 is available, the same labels decide class by class whether to keep its boundary or ours. Given the true masks of eight look-alike cell lines, SAM 3 assigns classes at Cohen's kappa = 0.038 and SnapHead at 0.754 (60 labeled images), and when only the class names change, SAM 3 falls to chance and SnapHead's score is unchanged. End to end, with 20 labeled images, SNAP beats a SAM 3 oracle tuned on the evaluation labels on five microscopy projects (0.484 against 0.441 F1), and run unchanged on five held-out datasets, it beats SAM 3 as shipped on four. Our results suggest that frozen foundation features already encode the class boundaries a generic vocabulary misses, and that a project's own labels are enough to read them out.

papers.title: Beyond Segmentation: Enriching ImageCAS with Coronary Ostia Landmarks, Rooted Centerline Graphs, and Open-Weight Localization Models
papers.abstract: Coronary ostia and centerlines are key reference points for automated analysis of coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA), from surgical planning to intraoperative vessel tracking. However, the only public ostium annotations cover 77 non-gated aortic scans, not CCTA, while CAT08 and ASOCA (32 and 40 CCTA scans) mark the ostia only implicitly, as centerline start points. This work enriches ImageCAS, the largest public dataset for coronary artery segmentation, with ostium annotations for its 1000 patients and centerline graphs rooted at these new ostia, making it, to the authors' knowledge, the largest public dataset for ostium localization and the only one with centerlines following the official ImageCAS masks and starting at annotated ostia. Three annotators marked each ostium in the first 500 volumes; in the next 500, the candidates of a model trained on the first batch were corrected (human-in-the-loop). Six 3D localization models, trained on ImageCAS, CAT08 and ASOCA, were benchmarked on 58 held-out volumes (50 ImageCAS, 4 CAT08, 4 ASOCA). SwinUNETR-V2 and nnResUNet localized all ostia without failure (>5 mm error), with median errors of 0.70-0.87 mm. Trained on CAT08 and ASOCA alone, SwinUNETR-V2 fails on 34% of right and 53% of left ostia, whereas adding 250 ImageCAS volumes removes all failures. The centerlines were extracted by a deterministic, quality-controlled minimal-path procedure; on ASOCA, they cover a median of 99.5% of the reference length, with a median per-patient mean distance of 0.22 mm between matched reference points and centerlines. Annotations, centerlines, code, and weights are available at https://hal9000-lab.github.io/.

papers.title: Intent-Aware Caching for Efficient LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Modern LLM serving systems use prefix caching to accelerate multi-turn conversational workloads. They cache the key-value states of previous conversation prefixes and reuse them when subsequent requests share the same prefix, to avoid redundant prefill computation and reduce serving latency. However, achieving a high cache hit rate remains challenging because cache reuse depends on whether a conversation continues and how soon the next turn arrives. Our analysis of real workloads shows that user intent is a useful signal for this behavior, as different intents exhibit different continuation probabilities and inter-turn delays. Based on this key insight, we propose Intent-Aware Caching (IAC), an online eviction policy that classifies requests by intent, learns lightweight reuse statistics from recent serving logs and leverages these statistics to guide an oracle-inspired eviction strategy. Extensive evaluation on real workloads (WildChat and ShareChat) shows that IAC reaches a 34.6% cache hit rate. This substantially outperforms both the previous learning-based approach (18.8%) and traditional methods such as least recently used (LRU, 12.2%), while reducing average serving latency by up to 46.1%.

papers.title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
papers.abstract: We give an exposition of OpenAI's recent result that the exponent of matrix multiplication is at most 9/4 valid over every field. Our main tool is a fractional symmetrized variant of the tensor value introduced by Coppersmith and Winograd, used in place of spectral points (tensor characters) in the original proof. We prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of this value on partially direct sums, whose summands share one tensor factor and occupy independent subspaces in the other two. Together with the degenerations of polynomial multiplication tensors from the OpenAI proof, this inequality yields the bound.

papers.title: Direct Regression and Geometric Recovery for Event-based Spacecraft Pose Estimation
papers.abstract: Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and dynamic range for uncooperative spacecraft pose estimation, but models trained on synthetic event streams must generalize to the noise, background activity, and contrast variation of physical sensors. We present a comparative systems study of two independently developed approaches to synthetic-to-real, event-based 6-DoF spacecraft pose estimation. The first is a modular pipeline that combines learned keypoint detection and unlabeled target-domain adaptation with geometry-based pose recovery and temporal smoothing. The second directly regresses translation and rotation from global and cropped event representations using an apparent-scale cue, physics-motivated synthetic corruptions, and feature-consistency regularization. We evaluate both systems under the same SPARK 2026 hidden-test protocol on the real-event split of SPADES, with predictions for all test frames. The results reveal a component-wise reversal concealed by the aggregate challenge score: direct regression reduces orientation error by 22.7% (1.1767 to 0.9101 rad) and obtains a 13.4% lower composite score, whereas the modular pipeline reduces relative translation error by 78.7% (0.1335 to 0.0285). Archived configurations and a qualitative failure case identify plausible explanations for these complementary error profiles, without isolating their causes. These findings motivate a testable hybrid design that combines direct orientation estimation with geometry-constrained translation recovery.

papers.title: How many points does it take to see the homotopy of a space? Minimal acyclic categorical models
papers.abstract: Every connected homotopy type is the classifying space of a small category, but this general result gives little control over the categories involved. We study finite acyclic categorical models and measure their complexity by the number of objects. Our main tool is the sink lemma, which describes the addition of a sink as the attachment of a cone along an explicit map. Using it, we determine the minimum number of objects required to model spheres, bouquets of spheres, Moore spaces of cyclic groups, real projective spaces, and lens spaces. We also exhibit infinitely many pairwise non-isomorphic rigid minimal models of the sphere. To include spaces admitting no finite model, we introduce a truncated invariant measuring the minimum number of objects required for a finite acyclic category to approximate a space through degree n. Spreading a finite monoid over n+1 objects produces such a category with an n-connected map to the monoid's classifying space. For every nontrivial finite group, this bound is optimal, although its classifying space admits no finite acyclic model.

papers.title: Row-sparse ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses with a few extra rows: local search with approximation guarantees
papers.abstract: For a rank-$r$ matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverses $H$ with few nonzero rows give least-squares solutions that are fast to evaluate and use few variables. A known determinant-based local search finds one with exactly $r$ nonzero rows and 2,1-norm within an essentially tight factor $r$ of the minimum at an exact local optimum. We let the nonzero rows of $H$ lie in a set $K$ of $k\ge r$ indices and study how to choose $K$. We bound the loss of this restriction (restricted over unrestricted minimum 2,1-norm) by a simple geometric certificate and establish that a local search maximizing the squared rank-$r$ volume of the corresponding columns of $A$ gives loss at most $\sqrt{k(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$, where $1+ε$ is the swap tolerance. With $ε=0$ this is $r$ at $k=r$ and less than $\sqrt{2r}$ for $k\ge2r$; with $ε=1/k$ the search runs in polynomial time on rational data. The same support yields an ah-symmetric reflexive generalized inverse with spectral norm within a factor $\sqrt{1+(n-k)(r+εk)/(k-r+1)}$ of that of the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse. The loss guarantees hold for every norm on the rows. In general, our certificate bound is tight up to a factor depending only on $k/r$, and on some instances, for a suitable row norm, so is the loss bound; for the 2,1-norm, however, the certificate can overestimate the loss by a factor $\sqrt r$. The local search is the Fedorov exchange algorithm of 0/1 D-optimal design; this yields a fast implementation and, via the Kiefer-Wolfowitz theorem, supports of at most $r(r+1)/2+1$ rows with certificate at most $\sqrt r$, best possible in general. On instances from earlier work, the observed loss is far below the guarantee, and the method matches two ADMM heuristics when few rows are removed and otherwise gives 2,1-norms up to 27% smaller, one to two orders of magnitude faster.

papers.title: Forecasting Fundamental-Plane Tests of Intermediate-mass Black Holes in Radio-selected Dwarf Galaxies
papers.abstract: A radio/X-ray Fundamental Plane (FP) test of an intermediate-mass black hole is informative only when the compact radio emission, hard X-rays, accretion state, and host association refer to the same accretor. We used published VLA, VLBA, \textit{Chandra}, and \textit{HST} observations of a radio-selected dwarf-galaxy sample to determine when present nondetections are constraining and what observations are required for a stronger test. The VLBA follow-up reveals that compactness alone does not establish association with the target dwarf, while for the best nuclear candidates the radio component relevant to the FP has not yet been isolated on the intermediate physical scales between the VLA and VLBA measurements. We therefore recast the FP as a forward question: for an assumed black-hole mass, how likely is a given radio observation to detect the compact core? The calculation includes intrinsic FP scatter, X-ray uncertainties, the radio spectral index, the accretion state, and source size relative to the beam. The existing VLBA nondetections have low completeness across the adopted intermediate-mass range and do not provide useful black-hole mass upper limits. Meaningful tests require deeper resolution-matched radio imaging, recovery of intermediate-scale structure, and contemporaneous measurements of the intrinsic hard-X-ray component. Because the calculation returns a mass-dependent detection function for each source, the same framework can be applied to larger dwarf-galaxy samples to quantify survey completeness and build selection functions for population studies of low-mass black holes.

papers.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
papers.abstract: LLM agents benefit from using memory systems to improve performance on long-horizon, multi-session tasks. However, memory introduces a critical attack surface. Malicious instructions encountered in one session may be stored and propagated through memory before being retrieved and acted upon in later sessions. Because memory systems differ in how they process and retrieve information, the downstream effects of poisoning can vary significantly across systems. To quantify the effects of poisoning across different memory architectures, we introduce MemoryDojo, a benchmark for tracing the lifecycle of poisoned information through agent memory and measuring its influence on subsequent agent behavior. MemoryDojo is easily extensible, consists of 155 multi-session long-horizon trajectories covering four domains, and supports five different memory systems. Through our evaluation, we find that all memory systems are susceptible to memory poisoning, with substantial variation in downstream effects. We further propose a memory-aware poison optimization process that increases the poisoning efficacy, highlighting differences between memory architectures. We hope that MemoryDojo will support research on understanding and mitigating agentic memory risks.

papers.title: FOSCAR: Accelerating Decode Attention over 2- and 4-Bit KV Caches through Affine Folding
papers.abstract: Large-language-model decode attention streams the key-value (KV) cache for every generated token. Packing that cache into 2-bit or 4-bit quantized integers reduces memory traffic but does not automatically translate into latency saving. Existing 2-bit fused kernels reach under 31%/15% of peak HBM throughput on H100/B200. Converting each value and applying its scale and offset before feeding Tensor Cores is a major bottleneck because instruction-issue throughput is scarce on modern GPUs. Instead of applying scale and offset to each KV value, FOSCAR uses affine folding to apply them to the other operand or the output of decode-attention matrix products, depending on the quantization scheme (token-wise or channel-wise). This reduces scale-and-offset operations by up to two orders of magnitude while preserving the dequantized attention output in exact arithmetic. FOSCAR also uses bit manipulation to feed KV operands to Tensor Cores efficiently, requiring only 1 and 0.19 ALU instructions per INT2 element on H100 and B200, respectively. Finally, FOSCAR builds warp-specialized GPU pipelines for Hopper (H100) and Blackwell (B200) using wgmma and tcgen05. On H100, FOSCAR INT2 and INT4 kernels achieve geo-mean speedups of $3.36\times$ and $2.83\times$ over FlashInfer BF16, and $2.03\times$ and $1.71\times$ over TensorRT-LLM FP8. On B200, the corresponding INT2 and INT4 speedups are $2.67\times$ and $2.30\times$ over FlashInfer BF16, $1.48\times$ and $1.28\times$ over TensorRT-LLM FP8, and $1.16\times$ and $1.00\times$ over TensorRT-LLM NVFP4. We integrate FOSCAR into SGLang to benchmark serving efficiency. On long-context serving workloads, FOSCAR increases peak aggregate throughput by up to 170% and 341% over 2-bit and 16-bit baselines, respectively. We open-source FOSCAR as a kernel library at https://github.com/FutureMLS-Lab/FOSCAR.

papers.title: Fixed-point acceleration on Neural Wasserstein manifolds
papers.abstract: We propose a fixed-point acceleration method for optimization over probability measures, applicable to a variety of machine learning problems. We represent probability measures as pushforwards of a reference distribution through a neural network map and equip the parameter space with the induced pullback Wasserstein metric. This geometric structure allows natural gradient descent to be interpreted as a fixed-point iteration on a Riemannian manifold. We accelerate this iteration using Riemannian Anderson mixing method, which exploits historical residuals to capture approximate second-order information without forming Hessians. In the present parametric setting, the manifold is represented by Euclidean coordinates endowed with a point-dependent metric, simplifying retraction and vector transport. We evaluate the method on multimodal sampling, PDE-based inverse problems, aggregation dynamics, Bayesian logistic regression, and generative modeling. Across the tested tasks, Anderson mixing reduces the number of natural-gradient iterations and achieves competitive performance relative to SGD and Adam in terms of both loss-gradient evaluations and wall-clock time. These results suggest that fixed-point acceleration is an efficient tool for improving the computational efficiency of training on parametric Wasserstein methods.

papers.title: Evaluating Anterior Cruciate Ligament Risk of Injury Using a Graph Convolutional Autoencoder
papers.abstract: Current solutions for assessing the risk of anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury typically rely on expensive motion-capture labs that require substantial resource investment or subjective evaluations of specific athletic stress tests by experts. The Drop Vertical Jump (DVJ) and the Single Leg Hop (SLH) are two examples of such tests typically used to track progress in ACL rehabilitation. In this paper, we develop an unsupervised learning model that runs entirely on a smartphone for two tasks, based on an autoencoder architecture with multiple layers of graph convolutional networks, which utilizes pose estimation data to determine a person's injury risk status. Our model accurately predicts athletes at high risk of injury for both athletic stress tests, with average sensitivities and specificities of 78% and 78% for the DVJ, and 75% and 74% for the SLH. Our findings support the development of a widely accessible smartphone solution for real-time screening of ACL injury risk.

papers.title: TriNetra: Thermal-Reliability-Guided RGB-Thermal Fusion and Tracking for Surveillance
papers.abstract: Visible cameras fail at night and thermal sensors fail under saturation, blur or loss of contrast, yet most RGB-thermal (RGB-T) detectors mix the two streams with fixed weights and cannot tell when one modality has become unreliable. TriNetra is a reliability-aware surveillance framework built around this problem. The proposed solution computes a frame-level Thermal Reliability Coefficient (TRC) from five label-free image cues, uses it to gate the thermal features of a dual-branch YOLOv8m detector whose visible branch, neck and head are frozen and COCO-pretrained, and passes the same score to a ByteTrack-based tracker that feeds a rule-based behaviour analyser. On the M3FD benchmark (2,940/630/630 split) the detector reaches 87.6% precision, 79.4% recall, 70.0% mAP@50 and 47.8% mAP@50:95 on the test split, with 17.0 M of its 42.9 M parameters trained. TRC stays near 0.78 on clean frames (standard deviation 0.012), decreases with the severity of thermal saturation and blur, reaching 0.53 and 0.69 at full severity, and is insensitive to RGB-thermal misalignment. With identical weights, the adaptive gate matches a fixed gate on clean data (70.0% versus 69.8% mAP@50) but keeps 43.6% mAP@50 when the thermal stream is corrupted, against 38.4%, 29.2% and 25.0% for a fixed gate, full thermal admission and a closed gate; the 5.1-point gain over the fixed gate has a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of +3.6 to +6.5 points. In tracking, the TRC-gated association performs on par with ByteTrack on a synthetic benchmark with exact ground truth and on 14 M3FD clips, and is slightly less stable under thermal saturation, so its measured benefit is confined to the detector. The limitations of the current evaluation are reported together with the results.

papers.title: Contrastive fine-tuning against stain and scanner bias improves robustness and downstream performance across pathology foundation models
papers.abstract: Histopathology foundation models achieve strong performance across diverse downstream tasks, yet their representations have been shown to encode scanner- and site-specific biases, creating generalization gaps and potentially limiting real-world utility. We introduce SPECTRA (Scanner and Pathology Embedding Contrastive Tuning for Robust Alignment), a model-agnostic contrastive learning post-training framework which explicitly encourages scanner- and stain-robust representations, to optimize performance and generalization on downstream applications. Using parameter-efficient LoRA adapters trained on matched multi-scanner and multi-stain whole-slide images sourced from the PLISM dataset, our method aligns spatially corresponding regions across acquisition conditions (scanner, stain), using other locations within each candidate condition as negatives. SPECTRA improved PathoROB robustness index, gene-expression prediction on HEST, slide-level classification AUC on CPTAC, and held-out PLISM retrieval for every model. Overall tile-level classification on THUNDER also improved, with exceptions for segmentation and calibration tasks. We open-source our training and evaluation codebases and release adapters and model weights for selected backbones.

papers.title: Consistency considerations for rare-event importance sampling
papers.abstract: We consider the problem of estimating a small probability $p = P(X \in A)$ by importance sampling with auxiliary density $g$, where $X$ is drawn according to some density $f$. We establish a simple necessary and sufficient condition for the consistency of the importance sampling estimator in triangular schemes where the dimension, the densities $f$ and $g$ and the set $A$ may evolve. It allows to refine the results of Chatterjee and Diaconis [Ann. Appl. Probab. 28 (2018), no. 2, 1099-1135] by establishing the exact minimal sample size required for consistency. Moreover, it allows to study the regime $p \to 0$ which, despite being the relevant mathematical regime for rare-event estimations, has received very little attention so far. We perform an in-depth study of the hyperplane case $A = \{x: x^\top u \geq α\}$ with Gaussian densities, showing that in this case, the optimal importance sampling density considerably improves consistency compared to the standard Monte Carlo estimator. However, we conclude the paper with moment considerations which suggest that, whenever the Monte Carlo and optimal importance sampling estimators both converge, convergence may occur faster for the Monte Carlo estimator.

papers.title: Extreme-value asymptotics for smallest enclosing balls of spherically symmetric samples
papers.abstract: Let $R_n$ denote the radius of the smallest ball containing an i.i.d.\ sample of spherically symmetric random vectors in $\mathbb R^d$, and let $D_n$ be the sample diameter. While the asymptotic behaviour of $D_n$ is well understood, much less is known about $R_n$. Starting from a classical result of Daniels for planar Gaussian samples, we develop a point-process approach to the asymptotic behaviour of $R_n$ in the three classical extreme-value regimes. We obtain limit theorems in the Gumbel, Fr'echet and Weibull cases, with the limiting laws described by geometric functionals of Poisson point processes. In dimension two, the Gumbel limit can be identified explicitly and is universal within the corresponding max-domain of attraction. We also study the asymptotic relationship between $R_n$ and $D_n$ and the supporting configurations of the smallest enclosing ball.

papers.title: Scarce or Missed Opportunities? Structural Peers and Latin America's Diversification Frontier
papers.abstract: Latin America's limited export upgrading is often attributed to failures to seize available diversification opportunities. We distinguish two possibilities: countries failed to realize opportunities demonstrated by structurally similar economies, or upgrading-oriented options were scarce within this peer-revealed set. Using export data for 105 countries from 1962 to 2024, we construct country-specific opportunity sets with an imitation-density measure associated with subsequent product entry. Latin America's deficit arose mainly from scarce upgrading-oriented candidates rather than weak aggregate conversion. Conversion rates matched the global benchmark, but regional frontiers contained few manufacturing products and almost no higher-complexity manufacturing candidates and, unlike East and Southeast Asia, did not shift toward them over time. An illustrative decomposition associates most of the regional upgrading-entry gap with candidate availability. The findings imply that industrial policy should expand feasible upgrading pathways rather than focus only on converting existing opportunities.

papers.title: SAGE-PAIR: Source-Pretrained Routed Residual Adaptation for Sparse-Feedback Recommendation
papers.abstract: Recommendation systems often enter a new serving window before enough outcomes are available to retrain the deployed model. We study this regime with 0.05-1.0% target feedback, a range that spans our stress tests while keeping supervision far below the degrees of freedom of the source recommender. At this scale, existing fine-tuning and meta-learning methods still estimate target-specific updates from extremely sparse feedback, leaving the update direction weakly identified. SAGE-PAIR instead transfers a source-supported residual correction space and only calibrates this space using target outcomes. We introduce SAGE-PAIR, a staged adapter that pretrains a low-dimensional global residual on an adjacent source period and adds a soft router over residual experts conditioned on source user profiles. Target feedback then calibrates this residual state rather than relearning the recommender. On a locked test split of KuaiSAR-v2, SAGE-PAIR (Full) achieves a 1.77% relative improvement in NDCG@10, while a core-protocol comparison shows a further 0.25% gain from routed experts beyond source-pretrained PAIR. Matched source-pretrained LoRA and Adapter-Tuning baselines remain near the source model, supporting the need for a different adaptation space. Thus, SAGE-PAIR improves ranking quality with millisecond-scale adaptation and inference costs. Sparse-feedback adaptation is fundamentally governed by the identifiability of the update space rather than by label count alone. Source pretraining supplies estimable correction directions for scarce labels, while user-conditioned routing contributes a consistent, differentiated cross-user correction on top of the global correction. Our code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SAGE-PAIR-610E/.

papers.title: Adaptive Budgeted Data Acquisition for Robust Off-Policy Evaluation from Multiple Loggers
papers.abstract: We consider off-policy evaluation when additional data can be purchased from several existing logging policies (or loggers) with heterogeneous costs per observation. While existing work on multiple loggers presumes a fixed number of observations from each logger, we study how to allocate a limited budget across them sequentially to evaluate a finite class of target policies. We propose Adaptive Greedy, an algorithm that purchases observations sequentially from the affordable logger that has the most cost-normalized variance reduction across the target policies. It turns out that each such purchase is an 'approximate conditional-gradient step' for the corresponding design problem. Under mild assumptions, we establish that the empirical allocation converges almost surely to the optimal design at an explicit rate. We also derive the asymptotic normality of the final pooled estimator and show that it attains the semiparametric efficiency bound. Simulations and a semi-synthetic application based on the AIDS Clinical Trials Group Study 175 show that Adaptive Greedy outperforms standard allocation strategies, remains accurate if stopped early, and matches the final accuracy of repeated integer programming at a fraction of its computational cost.

papers.title: One Run Is Not Enough: A Monte Carlo Protocol for Evaluating LLM Reliability on Data Science Tasks
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise for automating data science workflows. Benchmarks such as DataSciBench (2026) and StatQA (2024) have advanced the evaluation of their capabilities across data science and statistical tasks. Assessing their reliability requires examining both the quality of their responses and their consistency across repeated runs, task types, and difficulty levels. With this aim, we introduce DS-QA, a benchmark comprising 100 data science and statistics questions drawn from UK university courses, spanning 16 datasets and three difficulty levels. We develop a three-layer evaluation framework that combines general response properties (runtime, verbosity and text similarity), coarse-grained metrics (accuracy, code executability and completeness), and task-specific metrics. We evaluate OpenAI models using a Monte Carlo protocol with 100 repeated runs. The results reveal substantial variability in responses to data visualisation and supervised learning tasks, particularly at medium and hard difficulty levels, highlighting the importance of evaluating consistency alongside response quality. We also find that an increase of 0.1 in the word verbosity ratio corresponds to an increase of about 0.013 in the token verbosity ratio.

papers.title: What to Delegate, What to Preserve: Human Preferences for Agentic AI Across Everyday Life and Work
papers.abstract: AI agents can execute multi-step tasks on users' behalf, yet the boundaries of acceptable delegation remain unclear. We report a scenario-based survey of 289 U.S. adults with prior AI experience covering 45 use cases across nine life domains. Each respondent evaluated one scenario per domain, producing repeated measures of automation preference, trust, collaboration, AI leadership, privacy concern, and willingness to pay. Automation preferences varied substantially across domains. Generalized estimating equation models showed that greater trust in the AI agent, desired AI leadership, prior task-specific AI use, and anticipated financial savings were associated with greater automation preference. In contrast, concerns that automation would reduce personal fulfillment predicted lower automation preference. Open-ended responses further revealed a preference for bounded autonomy, with participants often favoring substantial AI execution while retaining human involvement, oversight, or final authority. We argue that delegation is best understood as a configuration of execution, collaboration, leadership, and authority.

papers.title: Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization for Efficient LLM-based Multi-agent Systems
papers.abstract: LLM-based multi-agent systems solve complex tasks through collaboration, but their growing, simultaneously resident key-value (KV) caches create a memory bottleneck. Applying single-model quantization policies independently ignores differences in agents' precision needs, potentially degrading collective reasoning. We introduce Coordinated Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization (CoMixKV), which combines online sensitivity estimation with joint agent-layer bit-width allocation under a shared memory budget. To our knowledge, CoMixKV is the first mixed-precision KV-cache quantization framework to jointly allocate precision across simultaneously resident agent caches under such a budget. The estimator derives sensitivity from a local attention-error bound using recent queries, keys, and values, without calibration data, trial quantization, or additional model passes. A shared controller combines these scores with remaining quantizable capacity and byte-level storage costs to minimize total estimated error. Allocations are refreshed as agents start or finish and new observations become available. Selected widths apply only to newly quantized blocks; recent states retain native precision and previously quantized blocks remain unchanged. Across four benchmarks and three LLM backbones at average 2-bit, 3-bit, and 4-bit settings, CoMixKV achieves strong accuracy against the evaluated quantization baselines. At the average 3-bit setting on Gemma-4-31B-it, it achieves 68.35% average accuracy, exceeding the strongest quantized baseline by 0.59%. On Qwen3-32B, it reduces peak KV-cache memory by 32.08% and achieves a 1.38x inference speedup over FullKV.

papers.title: Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman spaces are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider weighted Bergman spaces over open unit disk corresponding to nonnegative integrable radial functions with positive mass arbitrarily close to the unit circle. Then we show that Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on the weighted Bergman space are the fixed points of a normal unital completely positive map. This result generalizes the classical characterization of Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space due to Brown and Halmos. Moreover, we prove that there is no compact Toeplitz operators with bounded harmonic symbols on weighted Bergman space.

papers.title: Strong Convergence for Zig-Zag Products and Typical Spectra of Irregular Graphs
papers.abstract: We investigate the following: do existence bounds obtained by interlacing methods describe the spectra of typical random graphs? Depending on the model, we provide both positive and negative answers. We establish a Friedman-type theorem for zig-zag products of random regular graphs $G$ with a fixed vertex-transitive gadget $H$, where $G$ is sampled from independent permutations or matchings. We prove that the new spectrum converges in Hausdorff distance to that of the zig-zag product of the infinite regular tree with $H$. In particular, the new spectral radius converges to the sharp threshold established by Cohen, Cohen, and Maor. We establish the spectral limit using strong convergence and, drawing on quantitative estimates of Chen, Garza-Vargas, Tropp, and van Handel, obtain an $O(1/n)$ upper-tail bound in the permutation model. For the irregular configuration model, we show that the interlacing bound of Cohen and Maor, asymptotically $2\sqrt{μ-1}/μ$ for limiting average degree $μ$, is atypical: for uniformly bounded degree sequences with a nonconstant limiting degree law of minimum $δ\ge 2$, a random graph exceeds the interlacing bound by a positive constant with high probability. This gap is explained by the limiting spectral distribution, whose support edge is $2\sqrt{δ-1}/δ$. Strikingly, unlike the familiar behavior of random regular graphs, our experiments reveal second eigenvalues that remain far below this limiting edge even for the largest graphs tested. For $δ\ge3$, we propose that the scarcity of minimum-degree trees explains this behavior; estimates for their size suggest spectral witnesses within $O\left((\log\log n)^{-2}\right)$ of the limiting edge, which is consistent with our numerical observations.

papers.title: Metric Dimension Parameterized by Bag-Connected Treewidth and Bag-Connected Pathwidth
papers.abstract: The metric dimension of a graph is the minimum size of a set of vertices whose distance vectors distinguish all vertices of the graph. We prove that \MetricDimension{} is NP-complete on planar graphs of treewidth and bag-connected treewidth exactly three. The graphs in our construction have no induced cycle longer than four and have (prefix-connected) pathwidth at most four. In particular, the problem admits no XP algorithm parameterized by bag-connected treewidth unless $\mathrm P=\mathrm{NP}$. This answers questions of Bonnet and Purohit and of Bousquet, Deschamps, and Parreau. We prove that the problem is fixed-parameter tractable when parameterized by bag-connected pathwidth.

papers.title: GuardrailAgent: An Agentic Framework for Jailbreak Defense
papers.abstract: Despite undergoing safety training to align with human values, large language models (LLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that circumvent built-in safeguards and elicit malicious behaviors given by the adversary. Existing defenses are mostly static and fail to adapt to new or unknown attack strategies, providing limited resilience. To address these, we propose a multi-agent defense framework, GuardrailAgent, that offers adaptive, end-to-end protection. The system autonomously gathers and summarizes attack characteristics into a continuously updated knowledge base that supports both input- and output-side detection. A feedback module integrates misclassified cases for iterative improvement at minimal cost. Tested on over ten representative jailbreaks, the framework achieved a 93.1% input-side detection rate, 93.9% overall detection, and a 95.8% F1 score, while rapidly adapting to unseen attacks. These results demonstrate GuardrailAgent's outstanding capability to maintain LLM safety in the face of evolving jailbreak tactics.

papers.title: A Privacy-Aware Deep Learning Benchmark for Facial Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Facial Expression Recognition (FER) traditionally relies on raw RGB images, introducing privacy risks, sensitivity to illumination variations, and susceptibility to identity-confounding visual shortcuts. As an alternative, this work proposes a lightweight, privacy-aware pipeline using exclusively geometric representations-facial landmarks (478 points) and blendshapes (52 coefficients, ARKit standard)-eliminating persistent raw video storage. Six neural architectures trained from scratch on fused CREMA-D and RAVDESS datasets were benchmarked against an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50 baseline under a 5-fold subject-independent cross-validation protocol. Geometric models consistently outperformed the pixel baseline on unseen subjects with 12-124 times fewer parameters, while demonstrating superior robustness on subtle emotional expressions such as sadness. Ablation studies reveal that blendshapes capture the primary discriminative signal, while landmarks provide essential complementary spatial topology. These results demonstrate that compact geometric representations preserve affective semantics, eliminate downstream transfer learning dependency on visual backbones, and enable efficient, privacy-aware emotion recognition.

papers.title: 5G-NetBotSim: A Synchronized Co-Simulation Framework for Connected Robots over ROS and srsRAN-based 5G Network
papers.abstract: Connected robotic applications increasingly rely on wireless communication for teleoperation, coordination, and distributed autonomy. However, robotic simulators often use ideal links or abstract delay models that do not capture cellular scheduling and protocol processing effects. We present 5G NetBotSim, a realtime co simulation framework integrating ROS/Gazebo workloads with an executable, full stack srsRAN 5G network emulator. The framework provides isolated User Equipment (UE) robot contexts and stage level timing across the host, gNB, UE, ROS, and robot execution stages. We evaluate human to robot teleoperation and robot to robot leader follower coordination under controlled channel quality conditions. Results show how CQI and MCS variations propagate to throughput, communication latency, and robot performance. In leader follower coordination, higher channel quality reduces mean tracking error from 0.558 m to 0.460 m, a 17.6% reduction. These results demonstrate protocol stack in the loop co simulation for joint network and robotic-application evaluation.

papers.title: Safety Is $Π_1$, Provability Is $Σ_1$: One Framework for the Hugging Face Breach and OpenAI's Mathematical Proofs
papers.abstract: OpenAI's agents breached Hugging Face in July 2026, and the same company released more than seven hundred AI-generated manuscripts of mathematical proofs in October 2026. The first event is read as a failure in security, while the second is read as a success in mathematics. We read both through the hybrid framework of our paper (Kim and Kang, 2026, arXiv:2611.01914), in which coding, proving, and learning from data are derivations by one and the same deductive mechanism, distinguished by the kinds of premises from which they are derived. Under this framework, the AI systems behind the two events ran the same loop, in which a statistical proposer produces candidate exploits or proofs and a deductive verifier settles each one by a derivation. What separates the events is the logical form of the statement wanted by each of the two domains, security and mathematics. The safety of a program is a $Π_1$ statement, for it says that no exploit exists, which is not assured by any finite list of tests that have been passed by the program. By contrast, the provability of a sentence is a $Σ_1$ statement, for it says that a proof exists, which is assured by a single instance, namely a proof that has been checked by the deductive verifier. The theorem behind both is Turing's Undecidability Theorem: the halting set is $Σ_1$ but not decidable, so its complement is $Π_1$ and not $Σ_1$, which is to say that membership has a finite witness but non-membership has none. We prove that attaching a statistical proposer to a deductive verifier does not change this undecidability result, however good the proposer is. We then discuss what does assure safety and where the residual risk goes.

papers.title: Scalar Black-Holes in Gravity from Entropy
papers.abstract: We investigate static, spherically symmetric black holes in Gravity from Entropy (GfE), focusing on the sector in which the bosonic form-space field is a pure scalar. Starting from the full auxiliary-field equations, we show that the Dirac--Kähler matter equation contains both a scalar equation and a two-form consistency condition. The latter is automatically satisfied by a radial scalar. We derive an exact integral identity, valid for a general backreacted static spherical geometry, and prove that a regular scalar approaching zero at infinity must vanish if the sampled scalar and radial auxiliary-field eigenvalues are positive and the effective mass squared $m^2+ξR$ is nonnegative. In particular, this excludes minimally coupled static scalar hair with $m^2\geq0$ on the regular identity-connected branch. We also present the perturbative GfE vacuum geometry and use its curvature to identify the region in which nonminimal coupling can evade the sign argument. A second, sharper estimate shows that making $m^2+ξR$ negative is not by itself sufficient to produce a regular static zero mode: a finite interval of nonminimal couplings still admits no branch bifurcating from the vacuum solution.

papers.title: Witnessing Polarization Entanglement of Annihilation Photons via Compton Scattering
papers.abstract: Experimentally certifying polarization entanglement in annihilation photons is challenging because polarizers are unavailable in the high-energy regime and one needs to rely on Compton polarimetry. Previously proposed schemes designed for this task are either experimentally unfeasible or require a specific source state model. We address these issues by reformulating Compton scattering as a continuous-outcome quantum instrument, thereby enabling the prediction of the scattering angles and the post-scattering polarization state. Our framework allows connecting Compton polarimetry with entanglement witnesses by deriving experimentally accessible lower bounds on Bell state fidelities for arbitrary initial two-photon polarization states. We discuss how this witness can be extracted from coarse-grained coincidence measurements with detectors of almost any angular resolution. The presented scheme does not require knowledge of angle-independent empirical factors like detector efficiencies and source activity. Thus, our results provide a feasible route towards experimental entanglement certification in para-positronium decay with current technology.

papers.title: Autonomous Code Review: Hidden-Test Results on GitHub Issues
papers.abstract: Can an autonomous cross-provider review step change whether code written for a real issue passes hidden tests? We report a retrospective benchmark of 12 historical GitHub issues (five C#, five JavaScript, and two Python) from five repositories. Two directed author--reviewer pairs, OpenAI GPT-6.1-Sol and Anthropic Claude Sonnet 5.5, each ran twice per issue, yielding 48 planned workflows. A bounded terminal agent produced an initial patch; a cross-provider model reviewed it; the author model adjudicated findings and could revise the patch. The same hidden evaluator assessed initial and final patches. Forty workflows completed, while eight terminated before a complete evaluator outcome. Four completed workflows passed, and all four already passed before review. No initial-to-final pass/fail transitions occurred among completed workflows.

papers.title: Finding geometric criteria for negative eigenvalues of the Neumann--Poincaré operator
papers.abstract: Motivated by a question of Grigori Rozenblum, we study how the geometry of the boundary of a convex domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^3$ affects whether the Neumann--Poincaré operator on $\partialΩ$ has negative eigenvalues. First, we show that a flat face on the boundary of a bounded, convex Lipschitz domain produces an infinite-dimensional negative spectral subspace. For convex domains with $C^{1,α}$ boundary, we bound the number of negative eigenvalues from below by the Dirichlet eigenvalue counting function of a projected patch over which the chords are sufficiently short. A Rellich identity gives a sufficient condition on a defining function to exclude negative eigenvalues. We also report numerical computations, which led us to the theoretical results.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Benchmarking of Unified Multimodal Models for Shallow-Water UAV Image Distortion Assessment and Restoration
papers.abstract: Shallow-water UAV imagery provides centimeter-scale observations of benthic environments, but water-induced distortions complicate interpretation. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic zero-shot benchmark of unified multimodal large language models (MLLMs) for both assessing water-induced distortions and restoring shallow-water imagery within the same model framework. We evaluate five open-weight unified MLLMs with frozen pretrained weights and without access to paired reference images or descriptions of the true seabed. The benchmark contains 1,000 image pairs: 600 semi-synthetic UAV scenes created by applying synthetic water distortions to real shallow-water imagery and 400 fully synthetic through-water scenes. Three independent human annotations cover five distortion types. We evaluate four assessment prompts (P0-P3), from direct instruction to structured task decomposition, on all 1,000 images and four diagnosis-guided restoration prompts (R0-R3) on a common 100-image subset. Assessment varies substantially by model and prompt, with systematic prediction biases and a best pooled balanced accuracy of 0.654 for distortion presence. The best pooled PSNR gain is +0.255 dB, no unified MLLM improves pooled LPIPS, and some outputs alter scene structure or hallucinate content. Two restoration-only baselines also show limited transfer: InstructIR achieves a pooled PSNR gain of +0.040 dB, while PromptFix degrades all four pooled metrics under every prompt. These results show that recognizing shallow-water degradation does not imply reliable physical restoration and provide a reproducible baseline for future work.

papers.title: Research Collaborations Within and Across Disciplines in NIH-Funded Atlas Programs
papers.abstract: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) fund several programs (aka consortia) that support the construction of organ-specific or whole person atlases. These initiatives are designed to build comprehensive open reference datasets while advancing knowledge graphs, analytics, visualizations, and user interfaces needed to explore multiscale human atlas data. Here, we compare the Human Tumor Atlas Network (HTAN), Human BioMolecular Atlas Program (HuBMAP) and Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet) to examine collaboration by consortium component (CC) and researcher role and its relation to scientific impact. We retrieved 884 NIH award records and identified 1,255 focal publications acknowledging these awards, involving 8,952 researchers; compiled 99,108 citing publications covering 93% of the focal publications; constructed co-authorship networks; and as single-project publications or internal collaborations (IC), including intra-CC and inter-CCs collaborations. within each atlas program. Results show that IC publications are rare but involve many funded projects and principal investigators (PIs). Technology-oriented CCs tend to engage in intra-CC collaboration, whereas experimental-oriented CCs often collaborate across CCs of the same type. Compared with other researchers, PIs exhibited a significantly stronger association with inter-CCs than with single-project publications. IC publications have higher mean Relative Citation Ratios than single-project publications. Inter-CCs publications have significantly higher cumulative and annual citation levels in the first five post-publication years. Study methods and results can be used to inform the funding, management, and impact reporting for future Big Science programs that bring together 300+ experts from different disciplines to address major research challenges.

papers.title: Regime change in a model for political opinion dynamics
papers.abstract: Political crises involving a series of violent events are the rule rather than the exception in history. Here, we use a minimal opinion dynamics model to describe regime change as a contested transition between dominant shared ideas in a society. New opinions spread with a cumulative advantage, and agents do not return to opinions they held before, resulting in recurrent boom-and-bust dynamics without tuned parameters. During a transition, opinion changes grow approximately exponentially and then saturate in the finite system, declining approximately linearly as spreading is limited by the shrinking interfaces between opinion groups. We compare qualitative features of these transitions with historical data of political violence, used as an empirical proxy for contested transitions. A permutation test shows that violent events cluster in time in the dense Chinese and US records. Around their peaks, violent events rise in an accelerating way and then decline; in the Chinese data, the decline is consistent with the approximately linear decline in the model. We also use a fragmentation measure that serves as an early warning signal for transitions in the model. Overall, the patterns in the empirical data and the dynamical behavior of the model could contribute to a better understanding of long-term historical processes.

papers.title: Does DESI point towards transient cosmic acceleration?
papers.abstract: We investigate an oscillatory equation of state for dark energy that oscillates around the mean value $-1$ and includes a source term proportional to the cube of the number of e-folds. Due to this source term, the oscillation amplitude shifts towards the $w_{\rm de}<-1$ regime at higher redshifts, whereas in the future, the source term drives the oscillation amplitude towards the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime. As the equation of state enters the $w_{\rm de}>-1$ regime in the future, the dark energy density dilutes, causing the Hubble parameter to decrease asymptotically towards zero, so that the present acceleration is transient: the Universe transitions to decelerated expansion and approaches a static state as $a\to\infty$, without ever contracting. We compare this equation of state with BellDE, CPL and flat $Λ$CDM. We confront the model with a combination of datasets, including Planck, DESI BAO and three different supernova compilations: Pantheon+, Union3 and DES-Dovekie. We compare the log-evidence of each model with that of $Λ$CDM. The dynamical dark energy models yield $H_0$ values in the range $66.0^{+0.80}_{-0.79}$--$67.84^{+0.69}_{-0.74}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}$, with matter density values in the range $Ω_{\rm m}=0.3067^{+0.0073}_{-0.0072}$--$0.3271^{+0.0083}_{-0.0080}$ across all the combinations. These values are consistent with those of the baseline model, apart from a mild upward shift in $Ω_{\rm m}$ for the Union3 combination. Among all the models, BellDE yields comparatively stronger Bayesian evidence than the other models, with weak evidence for the Pantheon+ compilation and moderate evidence for the Union3 and DES-Dovekie compilations. The sourced oscillatory model yields inconclusive evidence for Pantheon + and Union3, while weak evidence for DES-Dovekie relative to $Λ$CDM.

papers.title: QAOA for Layered Architecture Recovery: Feasibility, Limits, and the Role of Decomposition
papers.abstract: Layered architecture recovery (LAR) reconstructs a system's architectural layers from its package dependencies, and is defined as a combinatorial optimisation problem solved with classical search. We investigate whether the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) can be applied to LAR, and with what practical limitations. We formulate LAR as a Quadratic Semi-Assignment Problem, transform it into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimisation (QUBO) problem in which each package is penalised unless it is assigned to exactly one layer, and encode it as an Ising Hamiltonian solved by QAOA. To reach instances beyond the qubit budget of a single circuit, we also apply an impact-guided decomposition that solves the problem as a sequence of smaller sub-problems. We evaluate the approach on three real Java systems ($15$, $18$, and $24$ qubits), studying the effect of circuit depth and sampling budget (RQ1), a comparison with a classical Tabu Search baseline (RQ2), robustness to simulated quantum noise (RQ3), and the decomposition (RQ4). We find that monolithic QAOA is feasible and accurate on the two smaller systems but fails on the $24$-qubit instance, that the sampling budget rather than circuit depth governs its accuracy, and that it is competitive with but does not outperform Tabu Search. Decomposition restores reliable recovery on the $24$-qubit instance, raising the optimal rate from $6.7\%$ to $93.3\%$; its accuracy is governed by the size of each sub-problem and, unlike the monolithic pipeline, improves as the sampling budget is reduced. Our results indicate that, in the current noisy intermediate-scale regime, problem decomposition, rather than larger circuits or more sampling, is the key to applying QAOA to software architecture recovery.

papers.title: Multiscale Closing Index (MCI) for measuring structural similarity between 2D point sets
papers.abstract: We introduce Multi-scale Closing Index (MCI), a new dissimilarity measure for evaluating the alignment of two 2D point sets. MCI is bounded between 0 and 1 and is based on multiscale mathematical morphology operations, with smaller values indicating greater structural agreement. The measure was motivated by the need to assess the quality of registration between point sets representing cell populations in biological images. To evaluate its behaviour under controlled conditions, we generated synthetic point clouds from Perlin-noise-based spatial structures, following established approaches for simulating biologically plausible spatial organization. We assessed MCI between those point clouds and different transformed versions, obtained by local perturbation, point removal, translation, rotation and addition of impulsive noise. Across these experiments, the dissimilarity MCI increased gradually and consistently with perturbation severity, while showing a clear discontinuity between clouds originating from the same underlying spatial structure and point clouds generated from different structures. We further compared MCI with commonly used point-set distances, including Hausdorff-based measures and Sliced Wasserstein distance. These experiments show the ability of MCI to capture structural agreement and quantify deviations between point sets, highlighting its potential as a complementary metric for evaluating two-dimensional point-set registration.

papers.title: Continuous wavelet-based feature extraction for laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy classification of human plasma samples
papers.abstract: Extracting discriminative features from laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) spectra is important for the classification of complex biological samples. This study evaluates continuous wavelet transform (CWT)-based spectral peak extraction for distinguishing human plasma samples labeled as SARS-CoV-2-positive or negative. Plasma specimens from 181 individuals, comprising 53 positive samples and 128 negative controls, were deposited as 5 μL droplets on silicon substrates and dried before analysis. Spectra were acquired using a nanosecond Nd:YAG laser operating at 1064 nm, with 100 single-shot measurements collected per specimen and averaged after intensity-based outlier rejection. CWT-based peak detection was coupled with a support vector machine (SVM) classifier. The reported leave-one-out evaluation yielded an accuracy of 93.00%, sensitivity of 94.67%, and specificity of 91.61%; these estimates remain provisional pending reconciliation with specimen-level predictions. Features identified by the CWT pipeline included emission lines assigned to Ca II, K I, and N I. The workflow provides a basis for examining spectral features associated with the studied plasma groups. Independent validation and assessment of specimen, substrate, and acquisition-related variability are required to establish generalizability and diagnostic relevance.

papers.title: Contention Resolution Against an Adversarial Scheduler
papers.abstract: In the classical contention-resolution problem, a set of players share a broadcast channel, and a player succeeds in a given time step if it is the only player to broadcast during that step. Implicit in the classical problem is the assumption that every player is free to act on every step: once a player arrives, it participates until it succeeds. We study what happens when that assumption is removed. In our model, an adversarial \emph{scheduler} decides, on each step, which subset of the players gets scheduled to participate in the step. An unscheduled player simply sleeps through the step. We measure a protocol by its \emph{efficiency}: the number of players divided by the expected number of steps in which at least one player was active. Our first result says that, so long as the players are given access to a global clock and to shared randomness, they can achieve efficiency $Ω(1/\log n)$. The players are able to achieve this bound without requiring any channel feedback, and even if the adversarial scheduler is adaptive. We also give a matching lower bound of $O(1 / \log n)$, which holds even with channel feedback, and even for an oblivious scheduler. Our upper bounds all require the players to have access to a shared global clock and to shared randomness. Our final result says that this type of implicit shared state is necessary. If the players have neither a global clock nor shared randomness, then no protocol can achieve efficiency better than $O(\log n / n)$; and this holds even if the other aspects of the problem are designed to be as favorable for the players as possible (the channel gives ternary feedback and the adversary is oblivious).

papers.title: Predicting fitness from genomic offset: a multivariate latent-trait framework
papers.abstract: Genomic offset methods quantify the genetic consequences of environmental change using genotype environment associations (GEA), but the conditions under which they predict fitness remain poorly understood. Here, we develop a theoretical framework linking genomic offset to relative fitness loss through multivariate latent adaptive traits under stabilizing selection. We show that squared genomic offset is linearly related to expected log relative fitness loss when averaged over genetic architectures, provided that direct environmental effects are absent. However, this relationship does not necessarily hold for a realized genetic architecture. We identify two complementary mechanisms that can explain high predictive accuracy of genomic offset statistics. First, when effective adaptive dimensionality is sufficiently large, the genetically mediated fitness response concentrates around its marginal expectation, reducing the dependence on the particular genetic architecture. Second, even with few adaptive traits, accurate predictions can arise from geometric alignment between the complete fitness loss matrix and the GEA metric. This second mechanism also encompasses direct environmental effects and their interactions with genetically mediated responses, which may preserve or weaken predictive accuracy depending on their alignment. We further derive bounds on predictive accuracy that characterize these effects. Our results clarify the assumptions and limitations underlying genomic offset predictions and suggest that genomic offset is best interpreted as a measure of genetically informed adaptive mismatch, rather than a direct predictor of realized fitness or any particular phenotypic trait.

papers.title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a family of division ring extensions and compute their left and right dimensions. In characteristic zero, we obtain a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture: a hereditary right pure semisimple ring of infinite representation type. For each prime $p\ge3$, we construct in characteristic $p$ a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram $I_2(p+2)$.

papers.title: Attractivity Implies Lyapunov Stability for Multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini Systems
papers.abstract: We study the linear multidimensional Fornasini--Marchesini recurrence with uniformly bounded boundary data prescribed on the open coordinate faces. Attractivity is understood in the sense of Pringsheim convergence, in which all discrete indices tend to infinity. We establish that attractivity alone implies Lyapunov stability, and consequently is equivalent to asymptotic stability, for an arbitrary number of discrete directions. Our proof combines inheritance of attractivity by lower-dimensional subsystems, a Baire-category uniform boundedness argument, and word-sum estimates to control coordinate slabs outside the Pringsheim tail. We use a generalized spectral stability criterion proved in a separate companion preprint, without reproving that criterion here. We also obtain a uniform exponential interior estimate and contrast our boundary/convergence convention with an earlier two-dimensional attractivity theorem.

papers.title: Drift-invariant kernels for discount curve models
papers.abstract: Kernel ridge regression estimates the discount curve as the minimizer of a pricing error plus a penalty given by the norm of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. By the representer theorem, the estimate lies in a finite-dimensional affine space that depends only on the kernel and on the cash flow dates of the instruments. We ask when this space is invariant under the risk-neutral drift of the discount curve, so that the estimated curves can be the states of a continuous-time arbitrage-free model. We show that this holds for every grid of cash flow dates if and only if the kernel is of the form $k(x,y)=\e^{b(x+y)}\big(c\,\e^{axy}+1-c\big)$, apart from kernels whose Hilbert space has dimension at most two. For this kernel the estimated curve is an affine combination of flat discount curves, each corresponding to a constant continuously compounded yield. The drift-invariant subspaces correspond to sub-grids of the cash flow dates, and the discounted coefficients have linear risk-neutral dynamics.

papers.title: Universal photonic synthetic temporal-mode converter for heterogeneous quantum interconnects
papers.abstract: We propose a synthetic temporal-mode converter (STC) that combines programmable waveform matching with denser time multiplexing for heterogeneous quantum interconnects.
